title: OmniLatent 1.9B 3D Model Unifies Geometry and Parts
summary: OmniLatent from HKU and Tencent jointly encodes geometry, appearance, and 64-part IDs in one 1.9B latent space, achieving 74.18 mIoU and 2.7x speed gains.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OmniLatent jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and up to 64 part IDs in one 1.9B latent space.
- Achieves 74.18 mIoU on mask-guided segmentation, outperforming P3-SAM and PartField by 18 and 22 points respectively.
- Runs 2.7x faster than separate pipelines at roughly 30 seconds per image with 8,192 latent tokens.


A joint research team from the University of Hong Kong, Tencent, CUHK, and Nanjing has released OmniLatent, a 1.9-billion-parameter multimodal[diffusion transformer](https://emergent.sh/glossary/diffusion-model) that collapses geometry reconstruction, appearance synthesis, and part segmentation into a single latent space. Officially launched on November 10, 2026, the model generates part-aware 3D assets from a single input image in one pass, eliminating the need to segment a finished mesh after the fact.


## Architecture and Performance


OmniLatent implements an MM-DiT with rectified flow that learns a shared latent space jointly encoding geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs. The 6-bit binary encoding supports up to 64 parts per object and, according to the authors, produces cleaner segmentations than RGB-coded masks by avoiding color deviation fragmentation during denoising. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-wt, the mask-guided model scores 74.18 mIoU for surface part segmentation, against 56.01 for P3-SAM and 51.93 for PartField. Without the mask prompt, performance drops to 62.42 mIoU, narrowing the gap over prior work but still maintaining a lead.


For amodal part completion against 200 ObjaversePart-Tiny samples, OmniLatent reports a Chamfer Distance of 0.03 holistically and 0.08 at the part level, edging X-Part at 0.04 and 0.11. Generation completes in roughly 30 seconds with 8,192 latent tokens, which the paper frames as approximately 2.7 times faster than running separate geometry, texture, and segmentation pipelines end to end.


## Training Data and Efficiency


The training regimen leaned on 900,000 meshes for geometry and deformation, 300,000 textured assets for appearance, and only 20,000 part-annotated objects for the segmentation signal. The shared-latent design allows data-rich geometric and visual priors to carry the data-scarce part learning, reducing the annotation burden. The system also exposes a point-prompt adapter for interactive refinement and an amodal completion mode for occluded regions.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially released on November 10, 2026, OmniLatent is detailed in a paper posted to Hugging Face. Xihui Liu of the University of Hong Kong is listed as corresponding author, with co-authors drawn from Tencent's Shenzhen office and CUHK. The release arrives amid a steady drumbeat of unified-latent 3D work, with 58 related stories logged in computer vision trackers over the last 90 days.


## What This Means


OmniLatent represents a shift from post-hoc segmentation toward part-aware generation baked into the generative process itself. By unifying geometry, appearance, and part identity in one latent space, the model reduces pipeline complexity and inference time while matching or exceeding the segmentation quality of multi-stage approaches. The 6-bit binary encoding and shared-latent training strategy offer a blueprint for scaling part-aware 3D generation without proportional increases in annotation cost, positioning the architecture as a candidate reference for next-generation 3D content creation workflows.
